academic_translation:
With a full mouth, making noise,
Or with the mouth wide open, one should not eat;
One should not sit with legs outstretched,
Nor rub the hands together.
translation: I should not eat with my mouth full, make noises, or chew with my mouth wide open. I should not sit with my legs stretched out, and I should not rub my hands together.

academic_translation:
In vehicles, on beds, seats, and in dwellings,
One should not be alone with another woman.
Having observed and inquired, one should avoid
Everything that causes the world to lose faith.
translation: I should not be alone with another woman in a vehicle, on a bed, on a seat, or in a room. By watching and asking questions, I should find out what upsets people. Then I must avoid doing anything that causes the world to lose faith.

academic_translation:
One should not indicate with a finger;
But respectfully, with the right
Hand in its entirety,
Even the path should be shown in this way.
translation: I should never point with just one finger. Instead, I should respectfully use my whole right hand. Even when I am just showing someone the way to go, I should point like this.
I should not wave my hands around too much. I should move them just a little and make a sound, like snapping my fingers, to signal someone. Otherwise, I will lose my self-control.

academic_translation:
Just as the Protector lay when passing into nirvāṇa,
One should lie down in the desired direction;
With introspection, to the thought of rising quickly,
One should firmly direct the mind from the very beginning.
translation: I should lie down facing the direction I want, just like the Protector lay when passing into freedom from sorrow. Right from the very start, I should use watchfulness. I must firmly set my mind on waking up quickly.

academic_translation:
Although the conduct of bodhisattvas
Is taught to be measureless,
One should certainly practice
The conduct of purifying the mind until one is able to practice it all.

locked_terms.use: way of acting of the awakening hero

translation: The teachings say that the way of acting of the awakening hero is endless. Until I am able to do all of it, I must certainly practice actions that make my mind pure.

academic_translation:
Three times by day and three times by night,
One should recite the Three Heaps Sūtra;
By relying on the Victors and bodhicitta,
One should thereby pacify the remaining downfalls.
translation: Three times during the day and three times at night, I should recite the Three Heaps text. By relying on the Victorious Ones and the awakening mind, I will clear away my remaining falls.

academic_translation:
Whether under one's own or another's power,
In whatever situation, whatever one is doing,
Whatever has been taught as a training,
In that situation, one should exert oneself and train.
translation: Whether I am acting on my own or following someone else, I should always try hard. No matter what I am doing, I must follow whatever I was taught as a training.

academic_translation:
That which is not a training for the children of the Victors
Does not exist at all;
For the wise who abide in this way,
There is nothing that does not become merit.
translation: There is no action that is not a training for a child of the Victorious Ones. For a wise person who lives like this, everything becomes a store of goodness.

academic_translation:
Whether directly or indirectly,
Do nothing other than the benefit of sentient beings;
For the sake of sentient beings alone,
Make a dedication of everything for awakening.
translation: Whether directly or indirectly, I should only do things that help living beings. For the sake of living beings alone, I give everything to awakening by sharing the goodness.

academic_translation:
Always, a spiritual friend
Who is learned in the meaning of the Mahāyāna
And who keeps the supreme ascetic discipline of the bodhisattvas,
Should not be given up even for the sake of one's life.
translation: I must never give up a friend who guides me, even to save my own life. This friend knows the meaning of the Great Vehicle and keeps the highest strict practice of the awakening heroes.

academic_translation:
From the liberation story of Śrīsaṃbhava,
One should train in the manner of relying on the teacher;
This and other words spoken by the Buddha
Should be known by reading the sūtras.
translation: I should learn how to rely on a teacher from the life story of Shrisambhava. I will know this and other things spoken by the Buddha by reading the scriptures.

academic_translation:
The trainings appear in the sūtras,
Therefore, one should read the sūtras;
The Ākāśagarbha Sūtra
Should be looked at first of all.
translation: The trainings are found in the scriptures, so I must read the scriptures. I should look at the Teaching of Akashagarbha first of all.

academic_translation:
Because what must be constantly practiced
Is extensively demonstrated within it,
The Śikṣāsamuccaya too
Should definitely be examined again and again.
translation: I must also read the Compendium of Trainings again and again. It shows in great detail what I need to practice all the time.

academic_translation:
Alternatively, for the time being, the concise
Compendium of Sūtras should be examined;
And those composed by the noble Nāgārjuna,
Both of them, should also be examined with effort.
translation: Or, for now, I should read the short Collection of the Buddha's Talks. I must also try hard to read both teaching texts written by the noble Nagarjuna.

academic_translation:
Whatever is not prohibited therein,
That itself is what should be practiced;
In order to guard the minds of the world,
Having seen the training, one should practice perfectly.
translation: I should practice whatever is not forbidden in them. To protect the minds of the world, I must see the training and practice perfectly.

academic_translation:
Regarding the states of body and mind,
Examining them again and again—
That alone, in brief,
Is the definition of guarding introspection.
translation: I must check the states of my body and mind again and again. In short, this alone is the meaning of guarding watchfulness.

academic_translation:
These should be practiced with the body;
What will be accomplished by merely uttering words?
By merely reading a medical treatise,
Will the sick be benefited?
translation: I must actually do these things with my body. What good is just saying the words? Will a sick person get well just by reading a medical book?

academic_translation: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the fifth chapter: Guarding Introspection.

locked_terms.use: Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero

translation: From Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero, the fifth chapter: Guarding Watchfulness.

academic_translation:
Accumulated over a thousand eons,
Generosity, offerings to the Sugatas, and so forth—
Whatever good conduct there is, all of that
A single instance of anger destroys.
translation: A single moment of anger destroys all your good actions. It wipes out what you gathered over a thousand great ages, like giving and making offerings to the Well-Gone Ones.

academic_translation:
There is no misdeed like hatred;
There is no austerity like patience.
Therefore, earnestly regarding patience,
One should practice meditation in various ways.
translation: There is no harmful deed quite like hatred. There is no hard practice quite like patience. Because of this, you should try your best to practice meditation on patience in many different ways.

academic_translation:
If one harbors a mind with the dart of hatred,
The mind does not experience peace,
One obtains neither joy nor happiness,
Sleep does not come, and one becomes unsteady.
translation: If you hold hatred like a sharp dart in your mind, your mind will not feel peace. You will not find joy or happiness. You will not sleep, and you will feel unsteady.

academic_translation:
Those who, through wealth and honor,
Have been favored and depend upon him,
Even they will attack to kill
That master possessed by hatred.
translation: Think of the people who depend on a master for wealth and honor. If that master is full of hatred, even those people will attack and try to kill him.

academic_translation:
Because of it, friends become disheartened;
Though gathered by generosity, they do not attend him.
In brief, someone with anger who dwells in happiness—
There is no such person at all.
translation: Because of it, friends feel sad. Even if he tries to gather them by giving, they will not stay. In short, there is no such thing as a happy person who holds onto anger.

academic_translation:
The enemy, anger, produces
These and other such sufferings.
Whoever strives to destroy anger
Is happy in this life and the next.
translation: The enemy of anger produces these and other kinds of suffering. Whoever tries hard to destroy anger will be happy in this life and the next.

academic_translation:
Arising from the doing of what is undesired
And the hindering of what is desired—
Having found the food of mental unhappiness,
Hatred flourishes and destroys me.
translation: Hatred grows when things happen that I do not want, or when I am stopped from getting what I want. This gives hatred the food of unhappiness. Then it grows strong and destroys me.

academic_translation:
Therefore, I shall completely destroy
The food of that enemy;
For, other than harming me,
This enemy has no other task.
translation: Therefore, I must completely destroy the food of that enemy. This enemy has no other job except to hurt me.

academic_translation:
Whatever happens, I
Shall not disturb my joyful mind;
Even if I am unhappy, what is desired is not accomplished,
And virtues will decline.
translation: Whatever happens, I will not upset my joyful mind. Even if I am unhappy, it does not get me what I want. It only makes my good deeds fade away.

academic_translation:
If it can be remedied,
Why be unhappy about it?
If it cannot be remedied,
What is the use of being unhappy about it?
translation: If a problem can be fixed, why be unhappy about it? If it cannot be fixed, what is the use of being unhappy?

academic_translation:
For myself or for my friends,
Suffering, contempt, harsh words,
And disrepute are not desired,
Because for an enemy it is the reverse.
translation: I do not want suffering, disrespect, harsh words, or a bad name for myself or for my friends. But for an enemy, it is the exact opposite.
The causes of happiness only happen sometimes. The causes of suffering are very common. Without suffering, there is no wish to be free. So, my mind, you must be strong.

academic_translation:
Devotees of Durgā and the Karṇapas
Endure the feeling of burning, cutting, and so forth
Pointlessly; for the sake of liberation,
Why should I not endure it?
translation: Followers of Durga and the Karnapas put up with the feeling of being burned and cut. They do this for no real reason. So why should I not endure pain for the sake of freedom?

academic_translation:
That which does not become easy through habituation—
There is no such thing whatsoever.
Therefore, by habituating to minor harms,
Endure great harms.
translation: Everything becomes easier when you get used to it. There is nothing in the world that does not. So, by getting used to small harms, you can learn to endure great harms.

academic_translation:
Snakes and gadflies,
Feelings of hunger, thirst, and so forth,
And afflictions such as rashes—
Why do you not see their pointless suffering?
translation: Think of snakes and biting flies. Think of the feeling of hunger and thirst. Think of itchy rashes. Why do you not see that all this suffering is pointless?

academic_translation:
Towards heat, cold, rain, wind, and so forth,
Sickness, bondage, beatings, and so forth,
I shall not be overly sensitive;
If I am, the harm increases.
translation: I will not be too sensitive to heat, cold, rain, or wind. I will not complain about sickness, being tied up, or being hit. If I am too sensitive, the harm only gets worse.

academic_translation:
Some, when they see their own blood,
Become exceptionally brave and steadfast;
Some, when they see the blood of others,
Become dazed and faint.
translation: When some people see their own blood, they become extra brave and strong. But when other people see someone else's blood, they get dizzy and faint.

academic_translation:
This comes from the steadfastness of the mind
And from the nature of a coward.
Therefore, disregard harm
And make yourself unaffected by sufferings.
translation: This comes from a steady mind or from being a coward. So, ignore harm. Do not let suffering upset you.

academic_translation:
Even when suffering arises, the wise
Should not cloud the clarity of the mind,
For in waging war against the afflictions,
Harms are many during the battle.
translation: Even when suffering happens, wise people keep a clear mind. They are fighting a war against troubling emotions. Many harms happen during a battle.

academic_translation:
Having disregarded all suffering,
Those who conquer enemies such as hatred—
They are the victorious heroes;
The rest slay corpses.
translation: Real heroes ignore all suffering. They defeat enemies like hatred. Anyone else is just fighting dead bodies.

academic_translation:
Furthermore, the good quality of suffering is:
Through disillusionment, haughtiness is dispelled,
Compassion arises for those in saṃsāra,
One shuns misdeeds and delights in virtue.
translation: Suffering also has a good quality. Sadness stops us from feeling superior. We feel compassion for those in the cycle of rebirth. We avoid harmful deeds and enjoy good deeds.
